---
title: "Data-Manager Identity and Tracking"
date: 2026-10-12
date-modified: 2026-11-09
---

**Status (2026-11-09): Design guide, revised. Phase A (identity and registry) is
shipped on jheem2 `dev`. Phase B (selection) is shipped for SHIELD: one committed file
declares its managers, read natively and in the container, and census has dated
releases built and checked in CI ([progress](#phase-b-progress)). Phase C1 is shipped:
since 2026-11-07 each step of the native modular SHIELD launcher writes a run record
naming its code commits and data-manager releases, and since 2026-11-09 jheem2 kernels,
likelihoods, simulation sets, and calibrations record the managers in use
([progress](#phase-c-progress)). The
target is now explicit binding (Phase F, [design](#binding),
[D-031](../decisions.qmd#d-031)): model objects are built under a named binding of
manager releases, which they record and which can be supplied again; it replaces the
planned exact-read capture (C2) and comparison checks (D).** Requested by the team on
2026-10-09: make specifications, likelihoods, calibrations, and saved simulation sets
aware of which data managers (name and version) they used, including several managers
at once and different releases at different points of a process. This page fixes the
target design, its phases, and their acceptance criteria, so the work stays consistent
across sessions.

**Revision (2026-11-09).** Phases A–C1 make the choice of data explicit and record what
a session loaded, but model code still reaches data through session-wide state, so a
record can say only what was loaded and a rerun uses whatever is in memory. This
revision makes data an input to building model objects: a binding of names to
releases, active while kernels and likelihoods are built, with the existing global
names kept as aliases that look managers up through it ([binding](#binding)). Exact
read capture (C2) and the separate comparison phase (D) are withdrawn: under a binding,
records name the managers used by construction, and reruns rebuild the recorded binding
instead of comparing memory with it. The earlier scope excluded changes to model code
and to references to manager globals; binding changes how model code reaches data, but
not which data a likelihood uses or any numeric result.

**Revision (2026-10-19).** The first version (2026-10-12) put selection last and
proposed recording exact reads first. This revision puts selection first, since it
determines which data a run uses and is the part the team works with directly. It
records complete-but-conservative context before exact reads, because a partial
trace of reads can name the wrong dependency ([recording](#recording)). It also
adds how releases are chosen in each application today and the hazards found. The
delivery practice is [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028).

**Verified against:** jheem2 `dev`
[`85b73171`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/tree/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e),
jheem_analyses
[`eb991798`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/eb991798),
jheem-containers
[`39649e9f`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/tree/39649e9f50e20ff25adc53b691fdf61bbd7266cd),
and bayesian.simulations `4e0d13e8`. Measurements are from shield2 on 2026-10-09. The
[binding design](#binding) (2026-11-09) is verified against jheem2 `dev`
[`f8f7322e`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/tree/f8f7322e) and jheem_analyses
[`e3a148de`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/e3a148de).

**Candidate durable home:** the engine contract (identity, binding, records) in
jheem2 documentation; declarations, loading, and the release store
in the jheem_analyses and jheem-containers READMEs. **Graduation:** when Phase F
ships for SHIELD, this page shrinks to a summary with links.

Related: [reproducibility contract](reproducibility.qmd),
[manager selection and compatibility](manager-compatibility.qmd),
[SHIELD container pilot](shield-container-pilot.qmd#current-installation),
[D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027), [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028), and

## Goal {#goal}

The work is complete when these hold:

- **R1 Select.** A run's managers are immutable releases declared in its
  committed analysis code, loaded once and verified, so code and data move together
  and container and native runs of one commit use the same data
  ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)).
- **R2 Identify.** A manager's identity is its content (a digest of the loaded
  file), with the release tag as a label when known. A manager changed in memory
  after loading is marked as changed.
- **R3 Record.** Every artifact whose numbers depend on manager data records which
  manager releases it depended on, stating how complete that record is: kernels
  (and so every simulation set), instantiated likelihoods, and calibrations. Under a
  binding, the record is the binding and the names the artifact used.
- **R4 Reproduce.** Deriving something new from an artifact (rerunning its
  simulations, transmuting it, or starting the next calibration stage) uses the
  binding the artifact recorded, rebuilt from its releases, unless a different one is
  given deliberately, which is recorded. Until that default is switched on, the
  active binding is compared with the recorded one and differences are reported.
- **R5 No behavior change** until a phase deliberately introduces one: numeric
  outputs are unchanged, analysts take no new steps, and artifacts saved before the
  change still load and run.
- **R6 Several managers.** Everything is kept per named manager, so a run that
  uses census and surveillance managers, or different releases at different
  stages or in one session, is selected, recorded, and reproduced for each.
- **R7 Bind.** Model code reaches managers by name through the binding active while
  an object is built, not through session-wide variables. The existing global names
  keep working as aliases that look managers up through the binding.

Not in scope: changing likelihood definitions or which data a likelihood uses; a
general artifact registry; stopping runs on a mismatch by default.

## How data reaches results today {#binding-points}

| When data is read | Example | Where the result is kept | Release recorded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| While analysis code is sourced | SHIELD likelihood instructions read national 1970–1993 totals ([`shield_likelihoods.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/shield_likelihoods.R#L229)) | In-memory instructions | No |
| Kernel construction | `create.jheem.kernel()` evaluates each element's value or functional-form function ([`JHEEM_kernel.R:156-160`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_kernel.R#L156-L160), [`SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R:5042-5108`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R#L5042-L5108)). SHIELD registers 26 such functions; they read the `CENSUS.MANAGER` and `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` globals. Kernels are rebuilt on every call. | The kernel, saved inside every simulation set | No |
| Likelihood instantiation | Observations are pulled from the manager passed in ([`LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R:929`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R#L929)) | The instantiated likelihood, saved in the calibration's control file | Indirectly (below) |
| Calibration registration and setup | `register.calibration.info()` keeps a reference to a manager object, by default the default manager ([`CALIBRATION_main.R:1576`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/CALIBRATION_main.R#L1576)), when the registration file is sourced; setup later instantiates the likelihood from that object (line 488) | The likelihood closure serializes the calibration settings, including the whole manager (line 608) | Only through the loader's attribute on the embedded manager |
| Deriving from saved artifacts | `rerun.simulations()` builds a new kernel from the managers in memory ([`JHEEM_simulation.R:119`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_simulation.R#L119)); transmutation builds a kernel for the target version ([`JHEEM_transmutation.R:326`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_transmutation.R#L326)). Interventions reuse the saved kernel (`JHEEM_simulation.R:2302`), but runtime quantity functions can still read globals. | Nothing; whatever is in memory is used | No |
| Analysis | Plots and analysis-time likelihoods read the default manager, including the outcome-location mappings plots use for observed locations ([`JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R:143`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R#L143); its callers are in `PLOTS_simplot.R`; corrected 2026-11-09) | Not kept | No |

jheem2 itself knows two things about managers: an object passed to it, and a single
default. The names `CENSUS.MANAGER` and `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` are variables the
analysis code agrees on, not names jheem2 can resolve.

### How releases are chosen today {#selection-today}

| Application | Manager | Release chosen by | Manager already in memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| SHIELD, native | Syphilis | `SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG` in [`shield_source_code.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/eb991798/applications/SHIELD/shield_source_code.R#L44) | Reused, with a warning that the declaration was ignored |
| SHIELD, native | Census | Not declared: the release the shared cached-metadata file names | Reused silently |
| SHIELD, container | Syphilis, census | The declaration in the captured source; the installation's census | Never (each run is a new process) |
| EHE and HIV ([`source_code.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/eb991798/source_code.R#L26-L40)) | HIV surveillance, census | Not declared: the promoted release, and the cached-metadata census, at load time | Reused silently |
| Ryan White | Ryan White managers | A file path in the local cache; no version | Not applicable |

Only one manager across these applications is selected by an explicit version.
Nothing records what the others resolved to.

### Hazards found {#hazards}

- **No content identity.** The manager object holds a name (for example
  `syphilis.manager_section3`, a build label), a description, timestamps, and a code
  iteration. Seven methods change its contents in place and update its
  last-modified time
  ([`DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R#L618)).
  The analyses loader attaches the release tag and SHA-256 as an R attribute, which
  jheem2 never reads.
- **One variable name, two managers.** `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` is the syphilis
  manager in SHIELD and the HIV manager in EHE, and both loaders skip loading when the
  variable already exists. By code reading, a session that sources EHE's setup and
  then SHIELD's would run SHIELD on the HIV manager, with only a warning. This has
  not been observed.
- **Selection at the wrong time.** Calibration registrations capture a manager
  object when the registration file is sourced, not when the calibration starts.
- **Timestamps as versions.** Two SHIELD helpers branch on
  `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER$last.modified.date >= 2026-08-01`
  ([`shield_specification_helpers.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/R/shield_specification_helpers.R#L138)).
- **Managers built from other managers.** The syphilis manager carries its own
  census-derived population (source `census.aggregated.population`). Its build takes
  census from the dependency bundle `data-managers-latest`, which holds the census
  last modified 2025-04-23, while SHIELD kernels use the census of 2026-10-08. The
  population a likelihood compares against may therefore come from a different
  census build than the population the model simulates. This is inferred from the
  sources and build records, not measured.
- **Scale.** jheem_analyses has 845 references to `CENSUS.MANAGER` or
  `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` in 85 R files; 32 jheem2 function signatures default to
  `get.default.data.manager()`.
- **Embedded manager, missing census.** For one SHIELD stage-0 city, the
  calibration's `global_control.Rdata` was 132.7 MB on disk and holds the whole
  syphilis manager: 2,471.5 MB serialized, against 0.8 MB for the calibration settings
  without it. Loading it took 9.5 s and about 2.9 GB of memory. The census manager is
  recorded nowhere.
- **Declaration read before setup's own pull (found 2026-11-09).** In an interactive
  session, SHIELD setup reads `data_managers.csv` and then pulls jheem_analyses, so a
  checkout that is behind reads the old declaration and sources the rest from the new
  commit. A checkout last pulled while census was `unpinned` loaded the promoted census
  instead of the 10.08 pin it pulled. jheem_analyses
  [#29](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/29) (open) stops setup when the
  pull moves the checkout.
- **Releases change mid-pipeline unnoticed.** One city's native pipeline ran stages
  0–1 before the syphilis release of 2026-10-09 existed and stages 2–3 with it; only
  log lines show it.

## Design principles {#principles}

1. **Data is an input, like code** ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)): selected per
   run, frozen within it, and recorded, not built into a runtime.
2. **Select explicitly, then record and check.** Selection decides which data a run
   uses; records and checks report what happened.
3. **Identity is content; tags are labels.**
4. **A record states its coverage.** A conservative record that may list too much is
   acceptable; a record that claims to be exact and can miss a dependency is not.
5. **Additive and backward compatible.** Saved kernels, likelihoods, and simulation
   metadata are non-portable R6 objects that carry their own methods, so objects
   saved earlier never gain new methods. New information lives in private fields
   read through package-level functions that treat a missing field as "not
   recorded".
6. **Behavior changes are explicit.** They arrive behind an option that is off by
   default, then are switched on deliberately ([D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028)).

## Design {#design}

### 1. Identity on the manager (Phase A, jheem2) {#identity}

A private field holds a provenance record, read through
`get.data.manager.provenance(manager)`:

| Field | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `load.data.manager()` | Base name of the loaded file |
| `md5` | `load.data.manager()`, using `tools::md5sum` from base R | Content identity, available for every loaded manager |
| `sha256`, `release`, `repository` | The caller, through a new optional `provenance` argument to `load.data.manager()`; the analyses loader passes its verified resolution | Release identity, when known |
| `loaded.at` | `load.data.manager()` | Load time |
| `modified` | `FALSE` at load; `TRUE` after any of the seven methods that change contents | The identity no longer describes the contents |

`load.data.manager()` already copies a saved manager through the current class
constructor, so every newly loaded manager carries the field. jheem2 imports no
hashing package; MD5 identifies content here, while integrity checks of releases
keep using SHA-256 in the loader and the store. Copies inherit the source's record;
managers created in memory have no file or digest. Two records match when their
SHA-256 (or, failing that, MD5) agree and neither is modified.

### 2. Named registry (Phase A, jheem2) {#registry}

- `register.data.manager(name, manager)` returns the manager, so a setup line can
  keep its global: `CENSUS.MANAGER <- register.data.manager("census", ...)`.
- `get.data.manager(name)` returns it, or stops with a message naming the missing
  manager. `list.data.managers()` lists names with their provenance.
- The default manager is unchanged. Nothing in jheem2 consults the registry until a
  later phase opts in.

### 3. Selection (Phase B, jheem_analyses and jheem-containers) {#selection}

Four steps, each small:

1. **Declare.** Each application keeps one list of the managers it uses, in
   committed code, replacing `SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG`. For SHIELD it is the
   plain table `applications/SHIELD/data_managers.csv`, so that the host-side
   container wrapper reads the same file without R:
   ```
   # Data managers SHIELD uses: each run loads exactly these releases.
   name,file,release
   census,census.manager.rdata,census-manager-v2026.10.08
   syphilis,syphilis.manager.rdata,syphilis-manager-v2026.10.09
   ```
   The names are what code refers to; the releases are the versions. A version
   change is a reviewable commit. A manager may instead be `unpinned`, which keeps
   it on its older release path (for census, the cached-metadata file natively and
   the installation's release in the container); syphilis must be pinned.
2. **Resolve and load once.** The application's setup loads each declared release
   through the verified loader, passes its identity to jheem2, registers it under its
   name, and assigns the existing globals. A manager already in memory is reused only
   if its identity matches the declaration; otherwise it is reloaded.
3. **Override, recorded.** An explicit run-time override (for example
   `JHEEM_DATA_OVERRIDES="census=census-manager-v2026.10.20"`) for experiments,
   stated in the run's record, so nobody edits the declaration to try something.
4. **Freeze.** The resolved selection (name, release, digest) is saved with the run;
   continuations and later stages reuse it unless a later stage deliberately selects
   anew (see [decisions](#decisions)).

**How existing code is affected.** Under selection alone, specification helpers
keep reading the globals, which now hold the declared releases. Binding (Phase F)
turns those globals into aliases that look managers up through the active binding,
lets specifications declare the names they need, and stores a calibration's manager
by name ([binding](#binding)).

**Containers** read the same list from the captured source instead of the single
syphilis line, so census follows committed code too. That requires census to have
dated, immutable releases (`census-manager-v2026.10.08` exists) and a publishing path
for later census updates.

### 4. Recording (Phase C1, jheem2) {#recording}

Records are stored on artifacts in private fields, read with `get.data.inputs(x)`
for a kernel, simulation set, likelihood, or calibration directory (`NULL` for
artifacts saved earlier). Calibration setup also writes a readable
`data_inputs.dcf` in the calibration directory. Each record states its coverage:

| Coverage | Meaning | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `declared` | The selection the run made (names, releases, digests) | C1 |
| `loaded` | Every manager registered or loaded in the session when the artifact was built | C1 |
| `bound` | The binding the artifact was built under, complete, with the names it used marked | F |
| `unknown` | The artifact predates recording, or a manager has no identity | Any |

`loaded` is complete but conservative: a dependency read while sourcing, before any
artifact existed, is still covered. It remains the record for code that runs without
a binding. Under a binding the record is `bound` ([binding](#binding)).

Container runs already record census and syphilis tags and digests in
`inputs.json`; the jheem2 records link to that run history rather than defining a
second one.

### 5. Binding (Phase F, jheem2 and jheem_analyses) {#binding}

*Adopted 2026-11-09 ([D-031](../decisions.qmd#d-031)).* Identity, selection, and
records leave one cause in place. jheem2 calls specification functions with only a
location and metadata
([`SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R:5058`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/f8f7322e/R/SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R#L5058)),
so they read session-wide globals; likelihoods take whichever manager object a
registration captured when its file was sourced; and anything derived later uses
whatever is in memory. Binding makes data an input to building model objects.

**Concepts.**

- **Binding.** A map from names to loaded managers that carry an identity. Its
  identity (per name: release, repository, SHA-256, MD5, modified) is small and is
  what artifacts store; the managers themselves are never saved with an artifact.
- **Active binding.** A stack. Application setup sets the session binding at the
  bottom, which takes over the registry's role (`register.data.manager()` adds to
  it). jheem2 entry points push the binding they build under and pop it on exit,
  including on error.
- **Resolver.** `get.data.manager(name)` returns the manager bound to `name` in the
  active binding and notes the name in the current recording frame. An unbound name
  stops with a message listing the bound names.
- **Aliases.** `alias.data.manager("CENSUS.MANAGER", "census")` makes the global an R
  active binding whose value is the resolver's result. Existing code (lines referring to
  the two globals: 317 in 40 SHIELD files and 961 in 101 jheem_analyses R files at
  `e3a148de`) then follows the active binding and is recorded without edits. Assigning to an alias registers the
  value under its name in the session binding, as assigning the global does today
  (committed code assigns them only in setup and tests); inside an entry point it
  stops. Aliasing a variable already aliased to a different name stops, which removes
  the hazard of one variable meaning two managers.
- **Release resolver.** jheem2 does not fetch releases. An application registers a
  function that loads a release from an identity and verifies its digest (for
  jheem_analyses, the existing release loader); jheem2 calls it to rebuild a recorded
  binding.

**Entry points.**

| Entry point | Today | Under a binding |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel construction (`create.jheem.kernel()`, used by engines, calibration setup, reruns, and transmutation; it evaluates every element function eagerly) | Specification functions read globals | Runs in a recording frame under the active binding; the kernel records the binding and the names used. A specification may declare `data.managers = c("census", "syphilis")`: construction stops if the binding lacks one, and resolving an undeclared name stops |
| Likelihood instructions (`JHEEM.LIKELIHOOD.INSTRUCTIONS`, the base of every instruction class) | Values read while sourcing come from whatever was loaded | Capture the active binding's identity when created; instantiating under a binding that differs for any name stops, since values computed while sourcing (national totals, error terms) belong to the binding they came from |
| `instantiate.likelihood(data.manager = )` | One manager object, by default the default manager | Also accepts a name, resolved in the active binding; runs in a recording frame and records the binding and names used |
| `register.calibration.info(data.manager = )` | Captures an object when the registration file is sourced | Stores a name, resolved at setup: either a name given directly, or the name under which the passed object is bound in the active binding (so existing registrations need no edit); an object bound under no name is kept as today |
| `set.up.calibration()` | Embeds the whole manager in the control | Writes the binding to `data_inputs.dcf`; the control stores the binding's identity and embeds a manager only if it has no release (F3) |
| `rerun.simulations()`, transmutation | Use the managers in memory | Take `data.binding`. By default they first compare the active binding with the record and report differences; with the option switched on, they rebuild the recorded binding through the release resolver (F4) |
| Setup of a later calibration stage | Not checked | Compares its binding with the preceding stage's record and reports a difference; per [D-029](../decisions.qmd#d-029) a change of data belongs to a new calibration code (F4) |
| Plots and outcome-location mappings | Default manager | Unchanged; the default manager stays for analysis ([D-029](../decisions.qmd#d-029)) |

Instantiated likelihoods hold the data they pulled, not the manager, and kernels
hold values computed from managers, not managers, so neither grows under a binding.
Interventions reuse the saved kernel; a runtime function that reads a manager
resolves against the active binding and is recorded against the session (SHIELD's
specification file references no manager directly).

**Records.** With a binding active, records extend C1's with coverage `bound`: the
whole binding, with the names the artifact used marked. Reproduction relies on the
binding, which is complete. The used names are exact for reads through the resolver
or an alias; a manager object copied into another variable before construction is
attributed to the session, not to the artifact. Without a binding, records keep C1's
`loaded` coverage.

**SHIELD.**

1. Setup builds the binding from `data_managers.csv` through the verified loader,
   reusing a manager already in memory only if its identity matches (Phase B's
   reload rule) and applying any run-time override as a recorded part of the binding.
   It sets the session binding, defines the `CENSUS.MANAGER` and
   `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` aliases, and sets the default manager from `syphilis`.
2. The specification declares `census` and `syphilis`.
3. Registrations are unchanged: `data.manager = SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` passes the
   object bound as `syphilis`, which is stored by that name.
4. As files are next edited: helpers and registrations use names; values read while sourcing move
   into instantiation (custom likelihoods already take a `get.data.function`
   evaluated then); the two `last.modified.date` checks become checks of the data's
   structure, with the helpers' maintainers.

**Invariants.**

- The same releases give identical numbers: kernel inputs for the configured cities
  that build, and a short container calibration, compared bit for bit as in the
  [Phase A gates](#gates).
- With no binding active, jheem2 behaves exactly as before.
- Artifacts saved earlier load and run; their records read as `unknown`.
- Behavior changes (controls without the manager, reruns under the recorded
  binding, stage checks) merge behind options that default to today's behavior and
  are switched on separately ([D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028)).

Binding makes visible that SHIELD's population likelihood reads the syphilis
manager's census-derived population rather than the census manager
([hazards](#hazards)). Switching it would change results, so it is a modelling
decision outside this work.

### 6. Beyond SHIELD (Phase E) {#beyond-shield}

- EHE and HIV declare their managers under distinct names (for example
  `hiv.surveillance`), retiring the ambiguous shared variable name.
- Ryan White managers get dated releases.
- Native loading prefers the shared release store over personal cached copies.
- Manager builds record the identities of the managers they consume, so the
  census-inside-syphilis case becomes visible.
- Each application adopts binding as SHIELD does (F2); aliases keep its existing
  code working, with `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` aliased to `hiv.surveillance` in EHE.

### Manager embedded in calibration controls {#embedded-manager}

Kept until F3: for managers without retained immutable releases, it is the only
kept copy of the data a calibration used. Under a binding of releases, setup records
the binding's identity instead and drops about 2.5 GB of serialized manager from each
control (132.7 MB on disk per city and stage, 9.5 s and 2.9 GB of memory at each chain
start). A manager without a release stays embedded.

## Phases {#phases}

| Phase | Scope | Repositories | Acceptance | State (2026-11-09) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Container runs take the syphilis release declared in committed code; shared verified store | jheem-containers, jheem_analyses | [D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027); installation accepted | Shipped for container runs |
| A | jheem2 test gate; manager identity; named registry; loader passes identity | jheem2, jheem-containers, jheem_analyses | Gates below; no output or behavior change | Shipped ([below](#phase-a-shipped)) |
| B | Declared list per application (SHIELD first); resolve, verify, register; containers read the list; census release path | jheem_analyses, jheem-containers | Native and container runs of one commit load identical releases for every SHIELD manager | Shipped for SHIELD ([below](#phase-b-progress)); the reload rule and recorded overrides move to F2 |
| C1 | `declared` and `loaded` records on kernels, likelihoods, calibrations, linked to run history | jheem2, jheem_analyses | New artifacts name every SHIELD manager with its digest; earlier artifacts load and run | Shipped: native run records 2026-11-07, jheem2 records 2026-11-09 ([below](#phase-c-progress)) |
| F1 | Binding, active-binding stack, resolver with recording frames, aliases, release-resolver hook; kernel, likelihood, instructions, and calibration-setup hooks; names accepted for `data.manager`; `bound` records | jheem2 | jheem2 tests on the toy fixture: two bindings in one session give two kernels with different values and records; instructions built under one binding stop when instantiated under another; alias assignment and double aliasing behave as designed; with no binding, records equal C1's; earlier artifacts load | Next |
| F2 | SHIELD adopts binding: setup builds it (reload rule, recorded overrides), aliases, and the specification declares its names | jheem_analyses | Kernel inputs and a short container calibration bit-identical to before; records are `bound` and name the managers each artifact used; native and container runs of one commit record the same binding | Planned |
| F3 | Calibration controls store the binding's identity, not the manager; chains rebuild the binding from the calibration directory; option off, then on | jheem2, jheem_analyses | Chains bit-identical; control size and chain-start time and memory measured before and after | Planned |
| F4 | Reruns and transmutation rebuild the recorded binding; later-stage setup compares with the preceding stage; option off, then on | jheem2 | A rerun after a census change reproduces the original kernel inputs; a stage whose syphilis release differs from its predecessor's is reported by name | Planned |
| F5 | SHIELD helpers and registrations use names; values read while sourcing move into instantiation; timestamp checks replaced | jheem_analyses | No alias reads remain on the model path; numbers unchanged | Planned, as files are next edited |
| E | Beyond SHIELD (above) | All | Every application's managers are declared and bound | Planned |

C2 (observed reads) and D (comparison checks) were withdrawn on 2026-11-09
([D-031](../decisions.qmd#d-031)): under a binding, records name the managers used by
construction, and F4 replaces comparison with reproduction.

### Phase A gates {#gates}

- **Tests run in the jheem-containers CI**, which already builds jheem2 at a chosen
  commit ([D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028)). A small test file in jheem2 uses the
  [toy fixture](../toy-fixture-spike.qmd) and a tiny data manager to check:
  - identity at load, the modified flag, and copies;
  - registry behavior and its error messages;
  - records surviving saving and loading;
  - objects without the new fields still working.
- **No numeric change:**
  - SHIELD kernel inputs for the 26 configured cities that build are identical
    before and after, using the comparison method of 2026-10-09;
  - a short container calibration is bit-identical to one without the change.
- **No behavior change:** the same launchers run unchanged, and nothing new is
  printed.

### Phase B progress (2026-10-25) {#phase-b-progress}

Phase B ships in three steps: B1 introduces the declaration with census unpinned,
so no run changes; B2 publishes dated census releases (planned as a script, delivered as
census CI); B3 pins census, announced.

- **B1 (shipped 2026-10-20).**
  - Container side: jheem-containers
    [#35](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/pull/35) reads
    `data_managers.csv` from the captured source (falling back to the syphilis tag
    line for older commits), and
    [#36](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/pull/36) binds new codes only
    after their check and keeps logs in the output folder; both are in the
    [2026-10-19 installation](shield-container-pilot.qmd#current-installation).
  - Analysis side: jheem_analyses
    [#11](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/11) (master `8f6815bf`) adds
    the file (census `unpinned`, syphilis `syphilis-manager-v2026.10.09`), reads it in
    the SHIELD setup with the same rules as the wrapper, registers `census` and
    `syphilis` by name, warns about a manager already in memory only when it is not
    the declared release or has changed, and updates the operator guide. `*.csv` is
    ignored in jheem_analyses, so the file has an explicit exception.
  - No change in data: natively on shield2, `ea3752f9` and the branch loaded
    byte-identical managers, and the native census is byte-identical to
    `census-manager-v2026.10.08`.
  - From master `8f6815bf`, a container smoke stage recorded census 10.08 and
    syphilis 10.09, and `calib.10.15` stages 0–3 and `calib.10.19` stages 1–3 pass the
    read-only compatibility check.
  - Regression checks: `applications/SHIELD/tests/test-manager-selection.R`, which
    evaluates the setup's selection block as written, runs in the manager-cache
    workflow on Linux and Windows; the wrapper's parser has unit tests in
    jheem-containers.
- **B3, early (shipped 2026-10-23).** A census update on 2026-10-21 changed the age
  dimension of the census manager's `census` ontology from single years to 5-year
  groups. SHIELD takes its single-year ages from that ontology, so its specification
  stopped compiling ("the dimnames of 'value' does not match expected dimnames for
  model quantity 'single.year.age.sexual.availability'"). Nothing checks SHIELD
  against a census before the cached-metadata file moves.
  - jheem_analyses [#12](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/12) (master
    `f30d2d7d`) pins `census-manager-v2026.10.08` in the file, and lets a census load
    that names a release come from GitHub Releases in ordinary sessions, verified by
    digest. Loads that name no census release, in SHIELD or elsewhere, keep the
    OneDrive path; the named release is cached apart from `cached/census.manager.rdata`.
  - On shield2, in a checkout that had downloaded the new census, the specification
    compiles and the C.12580 kernel builds with the pinned release; in the
    container, `calib.10.15.stage0` and `calib.10.20` stages 1–3 pass the
    compatibility check. Native and container runs of a commit again use the same
    census.
  - Moving to a newer census is a one-line change once it is published as a dated
    release and SHIELD works with it.
  - On 2026-10-30 SHIELD moved to the October 21 census's ontology names and set census
    back to `unpinned`; SHIELD's census loads again take the OneDrive path, unverified
    and unrecorded ([details](manager-compatibility.qmd#census-versions)).
  - On 2026-11-04 SHIELD's census was pinned to `census-manager-v2026.10.08` again.
- **B2 (in place 2026-10-24; first contributor build 2026-10-28; October 28 census promoted 2026-11-03).** Rather than a
  publishing script, census manager CI
  ([details](manager-compatibility.qmd#census-ci); jheem_analyses
  [#15](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/15), master `0845c7e1`) builds
  each census from uploaded sections, checks that SHIELD's specification compiles and
  an engine builds with the candidate, and publishes a dated release, marked **Needs
  review** if it removes structure or SHIELD fails. `census-manager-latest` started at
  the October 8 release SHIELD then pinned. The first master build (2026-10-25) published the
  October 21 census as `census-manager-v2026.10.25`, marked **Needs review**: SHIELD
  did not start with it. On 2026-11-03 `census-manager-latest` moved to
  `census-manager-v2026.10.28`, which has the same data and metadata as the October 28
  census that ordinary sessions then loaded from OneDrive, and on 2026-11-04 a contributor
  promoted `census-manager-v2026.11.04`, which drops the partial-year 2010 county deaths.
  Since 2026-11-05
  ([#25](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/25), master `02dc85d0`) a census
  load that names no release takes `census-manager-latest`, verified by digest; `unpinned`
  in SHIELD's file means the same; the HIV build takes census from a census release; and
  census is no longer published to OneDrive or bundled
  ([details](manager-compatibility.qmd#census-consumers)).

### Phase C progress (2026-11-07) {#phase-c-progress}

C1 starts with a record of each native run, kept in jheem_analyses, ahead of the
jheem2 records on artifacts.

- **Run records (shipped 2026-11-07).** jheem_analyses
  [#28](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/pull/28) (master
  [`b0680792`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/b06807920f9ef88181f48c3ebb7c516abc655058)).
  The modular launcher (`applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_setup_and_run_modular.R`)
  runs setup, each chain, and assembly as separate processes, each of which sources
  the checkouts and loads the managers again, so the code or a manager can change
  between steps of one calibration. Each step now writes a DCF file to `run_records/`
  in the calibration directory, named by step, chain, UTC time, host, and process ID.
  A record holds:
  - the step, chain, location, calibration code, time, host, user, R version, and the
    seed the step set;
  - the jheem_analyses and jheem2 commits and branches, with the tracked files that
    have uncommitted changes (for jheem2 installed as a package, its version and
    GitHub commit), and the versions and commits of bayesian.simulations,
    distributions, and locations;
  - for census and syphilis, the release `data_managers.csv` declares, the release
    loaded with its SHA-256 and repository, the MD5 jheem2 records for the manager,
    and whether the manager changed after loading. A manager loaded without a release
    identity is marked `unrecorded`.

  Failing to write a record is a warning; the calibration itself is unchanged. The
  records sit beside the MCMC `cache/` directory, which is all that jheem2's assembly
  and summary functions list.
  - Verified: a local modular run of `calib.10.15.stage0` for C.12580 (setup, one
    chain started, assembly) on jheem2 `dev` `f8f7322e` wrote a record at each step;
    the commits matched both checkouts and the census and syphilis digests matched
    the loader's.
  - Regression check: `applications/SHIELD/tests/test-run-record.R` runs in the
    manager-cache workflow on Linux and Windows.
  - Not covered: `shield_calib_setup_and_run.R`, `shield_assemble_and_thin.R`,
    intervention runs, untracked files, and which data the code read. The modular
    launcher refuses recorded runs, so container runs keep their `inputs.json`.
- **Records on artifacts (shipped 2026-11-09).** jheem2
  [#23](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/pull/23) (`dev`
  [`70857a6e`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/commit/70857a6eae2eb44198741575349c4a4c61d55bb3)):
  `get.data.inputs()` for kernels, likelihoods, simulation sets, and calibration
  directories, and `data_inputs.dcf` written by calibration setup, as
  [designed](#recording). They are the record for code that runs without a binding,
  which F1 extends with `bound`.
  - Verified: a local `calib.10.15.stage0` setup for C.12580 wrote a `data_inputs.dcf`
    whose releases and digests match its run record.
  - Regression checks: `tests/data_inputs.R` passes in the runtime image through the
    jheem-containers `jheem2_test_ref` dispatch (run
    [42654206996](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/42654206996));
    kernel inputs for the 21 of SHIELD's 32 configured cities that build locally are
    identical to `dev` `f8f7322e` (the other 11 fail identically on both).

## Delivery practice {#delivery}

Adopted as [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028):

- Work happens on short-lived branches and merges to jheem2 `dev` only after its
  gates pass; the team loads jheem2 from `dev` source, so a merge reaches every new
  session at once.
- Additive phases (A, C1, F1) merge when ready; F2 changes SHIELD's setup without
  changing its numbers and is announced.
- Behavior changes (controls without the manager in F3; reruns under the recorded
  binding and stage checks in F4) merge with an option that defaults to today's
  behavior, and are switched on in a separate, announced change. This avoids long-lived branches drifting from `dev` while the team keeps
  committing.
- New engine code goes in its own file (for example
  `R/DATA_MANAGER_provenance.R`), with small hooks in existing files.

## Rollout and risks {#rollout}

- **Cost.** One extra read of each loaded manager file to hash it (about 100 MB for
  census or syphilis); a few hundred bytes per recorded artifact. Under a binding, a
  function call per alias read. Two bindings with different releases of a manager
  hold both in memory, only when a session asks for both.
- **Compatibility.** Objects saved before a phase keep their old methods and lack
  the new fields; the package-level accessors return `NULL` for them.
- **Analysis code.** Aliases keep existing code working, so F2 needs no helper
  edits. Moving helpers to names and replacing the two timestamp checks (F5) happen
  as files are next edited, with their maintainers.
- **Aliases are implicit.** A global whose value depends on the active binding is
  less obvious than an argument; names in model code (F5) and the specification's
  declared names make dependencies visible.
- **Operator guides** explain reports when F4 switches them on.

## Phase B decisions {#decisions}

Adopted 2026-10-19 as [D-029](../decisions.qmd#d-029):

1. **Where declarations live:** one committed file per application, rather than per
   calibration code (for SHIELD, `applications/SHIELD/data_managers.csv`).
2. **Stages and newer data:** a pipeline keeps its selection; a later stage may
   select newer data only through a new calibration code, which records the change.
3. **Names:** one per manager kind (`census`, `syphilis`, `hiv.surveillance`, ...).
4. **Census releases:** dated releases published from each census update; until
   census manager CI exists, a small publishing script run when the cached-metadata
   file changes.
5. **The default manager:** kept, set from a named manager, for plotting and
   analysis.

## Open questions {#open-questions}

1. Whether the cross-manager census difference is material: compare the syphilis
   manager's census-derived population with the census manager's, for the ten
   SHIELD cities.
2. Whether chain processes need managers at all once controls store the binding's
   identity: chains run the engine and likelihood saved in the control, but the
   modular launcher loads both managers in every step. If they do not, F3 also
   removes the managers' load time and memory from every chain.
3. Where the release resolver lives long term: the jheem_analyses loader, registered
   with jheem2 (F1), or jheem2 itself.
4. Store-first loading for native runs.
